SCI.scope: Physics text, definitions, formula relationships and source-written task wording only; no figure-pixel or diagram-dependent answer approval
SCI.basis: Independent model-based reasoning, accepted source text and primary publisher references; source-validity flags alone were not treated as scientific proof.

checks.finding: Both languages preserve 'nearest' distinct same-phase points, not merely arbitrary points at equal instantaneous displacement. In a one-dimensional periodic traveling wave, a full cycle gives a separation lambda. The printed quarter-period example and all three numbered ball pairs are retained as source assertions; their Figure 70 geometry is not independently verified.

The longitudinal-wave comparison, both numbered ball pairs and Greek lambda are complete in ZH and EN. Wavelength is measured along propagation, not as particle excursion. Source subfigure б is consistently localized to b. Figure 71b geometry remains unverified.

Both languages retain the integer n*lambda exception and lambda/2 antiphase explanation. For the stated sinusoidal traveling-wave model, Delta phase=2*pi*Delta s/lambda: n*lambda is same phase modulo 2*pi, while lambda/2 is pi apart, with opposite displacement and oscillatory velocity. The left/right contrast is particle vibration, not propagation direction. This is a general model derivation, not an answer for adjacent balls in unseen Figure 70.

In one period the pattern advances one wavelength, so v=lambda/T. T=1/nu then gives v=lambda*nu. Both displayed equations, equation numbers (4.1)/(4.2), T, Greek nu and Latin v are preserved exactly. These are propagation-speed relations, not the speed of a vibrating particle. Paragraph detachment is a readability defect recorded separately.
The emphasized conclusion states the product of wavelength and vibration frequency, not a sum, inverse or unconditional speed-versus-wavelength proportionality.
The introduction announces two distinct periodicities of the traveling string wave; both subsequent parts remain present in the frozen text.

Temporal periodicity, sine/cosine harmonic motion, common frequency and amplitude, and phase differences are all retained. Common amplitude is valid for the ideal constant-amplitude traveling string model used here; harmonic time dependence alone would not imply uniform amplitude in a damped, spreading or standing wave. No generalization to those different models is approved.

At fixed time the wave profile repeats after lambda; with elapsed time the pattern moves rightward at v. Both languages keep the curve-through-O distinction and separate pattern motion from particle oscillation. Figure 72's actual curves and labels are not inspected.

The cross-page statement closes completely in both languages and preserves Delta t=Delta s/v. Delta s is the translation distance of the traveling profile, not displacement amplitude. The later curve not passing through O is preserved as source text without approving unseen Figure 72.
Both languages retain that equation (4.2) also applies to longitudinal waves. The relationship is not confined to transverse displacement.

nativeMechanicalLimitation.explanation: The captured native command fails because NUMBER uses word-character boundaries: Chinese 图70/图72 is not counted as a bare number, while idiomatic English 'Figure 70'/'Figure 72' is counted. These three digit occurrences are the same source figure identifiers, not numerical changes. Suffixed references such as 70e are handled differently by the same regex. Pure number_signature inspection reproduces the mismatches without executing the gate. A later concurrent edition.py change is recorded separately; this review does not certify its new validation behavior or convert the original failure to PASS.
